checklist.summary: Request time by email to Kim Wood, copying opposing counsel; provide case number/style, motion and time information. Coordinate parties, obtain JA confirmation before noticing, and use Central time. Pro se no-response and added-motion qualifications are retained in the linked manual.

Generally certify a good-faith attempt before filing; unanswered email alone is insufficient. Preserve the manual’s dispositive, emergency-contact, posttrial/postjudgment and curable technical-dismissal qualifications (p4).

Use the e-filing portal unless Judge Campbell grants an email request. Submit a PDF cover letter stating agreement status and a Word order in the specified format; retain the nonregistered-party service requirement.

Use the JA-provided OneDrive link; previously filed documents generally need not be resubmitted, subject to the manual’s accessibility exception. Do not email hearing materials. Small claims has a bring-to-court/provide-other-party exception; timing and hard-copy wording conflicts are recorded separately.

In-person default for matters not set as of the update; remote appearance requires a written motion and court permission. JA provides connection details. Video is required unless impossible; attorneys appear in person for trials.

Email JA for date requests/confirmation, not counsel’s coordination chains; email filed notices and cancellations. Court-ordered hearings require court approval to cancel; contingent settlement language must be agreed before requesting removal.

citations.quote:
Civil - Submission of Proposed Orders 
1. All proposed orders must be submitted via the e-filing portal or via email if a request
for such is granted by Judge Campbell.
2. All proposed orders must include a cover letter in . pdf format. The cover letter
should indicate whether the proposed order is agreed to by opposing counsel/party or
not.
3. Only the cover letter and proposed order should be submitted via the e-filing
portal. Copies of motions, responses, exhibits, case law or other items should not be
included with the cover letter or uploaded in the e-filing portal (see Submission of
Hearing Materials, infra).
4.
All proposed orders must be submitted in Word format. Counsel and parties
preparing orders are directed to remove any hidden formatting or codes. Failure
to remove hidden formatting may result in the order being rejected.
5. All proposed orders must be in DJCMA format (see #6 & 7 below), but
counsel/parties are directed to omit the service portion for the judicial assistant
to sign and certify service of the order (the Mand A portions of the DJCMA
format). Don't forget the four D's and the four J's.
6. Proposed orders do not need to include the addresses or email addresses of recipients
of the order at the end. A copy of the signed order will be served on all
counsel/parties registered for service via the e-portal.
7. If the case involves a pro se party who is not registered to receive filings from the e­
portal, the proposed order shall include as the last paragraph (before DONE AND
ORDERED) the following statement:
Counsel who submitted this proposed order to the Court for 
approval shall serve a copy of this Order on any party not registered 
to receive service via the Comt's e-portal. 
Counsel receiving the served copy of an order entered is then charged with 
responsibility for serving (via mail or email) a copy of the signed order on any party 
not registered to receive service via the e-portal. 
8. A memo with instructions on submission of proposed orders and the DJCMA format
can be accessed by clicking: Microsoft Word - Memo-Submission of Proposed 
Orders to Judiciary .doc (flcourts.org)
8
